description: Per-ID presentation and ordering metadata for the character-select and visual-lobby/ranking UIs: row identity, main-list order (and -1 hide sentinel), visual-lobby/ranking order, and a flag that requests an extra list-item X offset. CP_000 is a synthetic random-select entry, not a playable character row.

ID.simple: Row key, normally the CharacterSelect id pointed to by Character::Id_CharacterSelect; CP_000 is the separate random-select entry.
ID.technical: FName row key at offset +0x8 (export column 'ID', ImportKeyField='Id'). In the export all 27 non-CP_000 keys are referenced exactly once by Character::Id_CharacterSelect. CharacterSelect_FindRow (retail 0x1508460) walks DTM CharacterSelectDataTables (+0x450) and returns the first FindRow hit; it rejects NAME_None only when bCheckNone=true, and bUnused is ignored. BuildListData looks up the literal FName CP_000 to create the 'random' entry and dereferences that result without a null check.

PlacementIndex.simple: Zero-based order in the main character-select list; exactly -1 removes a Character row from that list.
PlacementIndex.technical: int32 at row +0x10 (unitless ordinal; constructor default 0). BuildListData (retail 0x1506740) drops Character rows whose Select lookup misses or whose PlacementIndex == -1, then TArray::Sort ascending by this value (the comparator's 0 fallback for a missing row is unreachable after that filter). GameCharacter_PickRandomId (0x12fd200) uses a different test: it skips a missing Select row, PlacementIndex < 0, and ids in Exclude via Exclude.Contains(Select->Id) (the Select row key, equal to the Character id in this export). The export has unique values 0..27; CP_000's 27 is never compared by the main sort because CP_000 has no Character row and is appended after the sorted entries. No exported row uses the -1 hide sentinel.

VisualLobbyPlacementIndex.simple: Zero-based ordering ordinal for visual-lobby, free-battle team and ranking character lists; it is not itself a C++ exclusion flag.
VisualLobbyPlacementIndex.technical: int32 at row +0x14 (constructor default 0). The visual-lobby top widget, free-battle team select and GameCharacter_GetOrderedSelectableIds (0x13081e0) build TMap<CharacterId, index> and ValueSort ascending; Next/PreviousSelectableId consume that order. Ranking's BuildCharacterFilters (0x16377f0) uses StableSort and substitutes MAX_int32 when a Select row is missing. None of these C++ paths tests the index sign: a negative value would sort first if it entered those maps, while CP_000's -1 never does because no Character row references CP_000 and the random item is appended separately. Export values are unique: -1 only on CP_000, otherwise 0..26.

bUseListItemLeftPadding.simple: Flag requesting an extra X offset on a character-select list item; the offset size itself is a widget property, not a table field.
bUseListItemLeftPadding.technical: bool at row +0x18 in the retail game build (constructor default false; export 14 true and 14 false). BuildListData copies it into UGameCharacterSelectCharacterListData::LeftPadding as ListItemLeftPaddingSize when true, else 0.0f; the CP_000 row is read the same way for the random item. SetupFromData (0x1519080) adds LeftPadding to the saved BaseRenderTranslation.X only when a base translation is set. ListItemLeftPaddingSize (widget +0x568) gets no store in the C++ constructor (0x14a4440), so its effective layout-unit magnitude depends on widget defaults not verified here.

notes: Export contains one asset with 28 rows: 27 per-character keys, each referenced once by Character::Id_CharacterSelect in CharacterDataTable's 48 rows (21 Character rows have Id_CharacterSelect=None), plus CP_000 with no Character row. PlacementIndex 0..27 and VisualLobbyPlacementIndex -1..26 are unique.

Consumer conditions differ: the main select list removes only PlacementIndex == -1; GameCharacter_PickRandomId skips PlacementIndex < 0 and excludes by Select->Id; visual-lobby/ordered-selectable/ranking paths require a resolvable Select row but never test the index sign (ranking uses MAX_int32 for a missing row).

Row-constructor defaults are PlacementIndex=0, VisualLobbyPlacementIndex=0 and bUseListItemLeftPadding=false; Id has no explicit initializer (FName default None). The two indices are ordinals, not times or distances; this row struct has no arrays.

The reconstruction loads one CharacterSelectDataTable loader into DTM +0x450, while the finder APIs accept a table array and return the first matching row. AGameCharacter also caches the optional SelectRow at +0x3C0; no C++ reader of that cache was found in the reconstruction.
Reconstructed C++ with cited retail RVAs/offsets; retail Blueprint graphs and widget default values were not inspected, and no byte-identical matching claim is made.

usages.detail: CharacterSelect_FindRow returns the first matching row in DTM +0x450, with optional None rejection.
BuildListData filters Character rows on a missing Select row or PlacementIndex == -1, sorts ascending by PlacementIndex, and reads the padding flag.
Reads CP_000's own row for the appended random-select entry, including its padding flag.
SetupFromData applies the resolved LeftPadding to the item's saved BaseRenderTranslation.X.
GameCharacter_GetOrderedSelectableIds orders owned/selectable ids by VisualLobbyPlacementIndex; Next/PreviousSelectableId reuse that order.
GameCharacter_PickRandomId uses PlacementIndex >= 0 and Select row key against Exclude before a uniform random pick.
Visual-lobby icons are sorted by the visual-lobby index of each selectable Character row.
Free-battle team icons use the same visual-lobby index ordering.
Ranking character filters stable-sort by this index, with MAX_int32 for a missing Select row.
Character setup optionally caches the resolved row on AGameCharacter::SelectRow (+0x3C0).
